releases.title: Agent Team Starter Kit
releases.summary: A configurable starter for coordinating specialized AI agents around a visible GitHub Issues work queue, outcome gates, and reviewable execution.
releases.originalState: Complex work can arrive as an unstructured request with unclear ownership, hidden handoffs, and no durable record of what each specialist contributed.
releases.delivered: The public starter kit packages a GitHub Issues queue, configurable specialist personas, orchestration through Azure Functions and Azure OpenAI, and explicit gates around the work.
releases.outcome: The pattern is designed to make multi-agent work easier to assign, inspect, and govern while keeping the work item and its history visible to people.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: clearer ownership, inspectable handoffs, and human-visible outcome gates for multi-agent work.

capabilities: Uses GitHub Issues as a durable, visible queue for agent work.
Separates work across configurable specialist agent roles.
Packages orchestration components for Azure Functions and Azure OpenAI.
Makes outcomes and handoffs reviewable before work is treated as complete.

architecture.label: Issue
architecture.detail: A GitHub issue holds the request, context, and visible work state.

architecture.label: Orchestrator
architecture.detail: An Azure Functions control layer routes work to configured specialists.

architecture.label: Agent team
architecture.detail: Specialized agents contribute bounded parts of the outcome.

architecture.label: Human gate
architecture.detail: A person can inspect the work record and decide whether the outcome is acceptable.

guardrails: GitHub keeps the request, discussion, and resulting work visible rather than hiding them in a transient chat.
Specialist roles and outcome gates can be configured for the workflow instead of granting one agent an undefined remit.
People remain responsible for reviewing consequential outputs and deployment choices.
limitations: This is a starter kit, not a production service or a guarantee of agent accuracy.
Deployers must supply and secure their own Azure resources, identities, model access, and repository permissions.
Evaluation, monitoring, cost controls, and domain-specific safety checks still need to be designed for each use.

provenance.label: Agent Team Starter Kit public repository
provenance.note: Public README, architecture guidance, workflow files, and source are the evidence base for this entry.

visual.alt: A GitHub issue moves through an orchestrator and specialist agent team to a human outcome gate.

article.title: Making multi-agent work visible
article.dek: A public starter kit uses GitHub Issues as the control surface for specialist agents, explicit handoffs, and human-reviewed outcomes.

releases.title: Customer 360 for Entities
releases.summary: An adaptive Dynamics 365 and Dataverse web resource that brings related operational context into the forms where work already happens.
releases.originalState: A person working in a business record can have to open multiple forms or related lists to assemble the cases, orders, entitlements, contacts, and other context needed for the next action.
releases.delivered: The public solution provides an adaptive JavaScript web resource for Dynamics 365 and Dataverse forms that retrieves and presents related entity context in one place.
releases.outcome: The design is intended to reduce context switching and make the surrounding record history easier to scan before a person chooses the next action.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: less navigation between related records and a more coherent operational view at the point of work.

capabilities: Embeds a reusable web resource in Dynamics 365 or Dataverse model-driven forms.
Presents related entity information such as cases, orders, entitlements, and contacts.
Adapts the view to the current record and available related data.
Keeps the user in the host business application while they review context.

architecture.label: Current record
architecture.detail: A model-driven form supplies the current entity and record context.

architecture.label: Web resource
architecture.detail: Client-side JavaScript initializes the adaptive experience.

architecture.label: Dataverse
architecture.detail: Approved queries retrieve related operational records.

architecture.label: User action
architecture.detail: The person reviews the unified context and remains responsible for the next action.

guardrails: The experience uses the host application's identity and Dataverse permissions rather than creating a separate authority boundary.
The component presents context; it does not replace the person's judgment or automatically commit consequential changes.
Deployers must limit queries and displayed fields to information users are already authorized to access.
limitations: The solution requires configuration for each Dataverse schema, form, and relationship set.
Performance depends on query design, related-record volume, and the host environment.
The public repository is a community solution and not a Microsoft-supported product.

provenance.label: Customer 360 for Entities public repository
provenance.note: Public README, deployment guidance, web-resource source, and solution files are the evidence base for this entry.

visual.alt: A model-driven form passes record context to a web resource, which retrieves related Dataverse data for user review.

article.title: Bring the surrounding record into the work
article.dek: An adaptive form component assembles related Dataverse context without turning context gathering into another application.

releases.title: Freight Triage Control Tower
releases.summary: A public Power Platform prototype that turns flagged shipment signals into owned, visible triage work with queue, aging, detail, and resolution views.
releases.originalState: Exception signals can remain trapped in email and ad hoc follow-up, making ownership, age, priority, and resolution status difficult to see across an operations team.
releases.delivered: The public prototype packages an exception intake pattern, Dataverse-backed work queue, Power Apps control-tower views, and Copilot Studio-assisted triage around synthetic freight scenarios.
releases.outcome: The design is intended to turn scattered exception signals into explicit work items with visible ownership and service-level context.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: a shared queue for freight exceptions with clearer ownership, aging, priority, and resolution state.

capabilities: Converts a flagged operational signal into a structured triage item.
Shows queue, item detail, aging, and resolution views.
Uses Dataverse as the visible system of record for the prototype workflow.
Demonstrates Copilot Studio assistance without removing the operations owner.

architecture.label: Exception signal
architecture.detail: A flagged shipment message or synthetic event starts the triage pattern.

architecture.label: Structured intake
architecture.detail: Flow logic captures the signal as a Dataverse work item.

architecture.label: Control tower
architecture.detail: Power Apps views expose queue, age, priority, detail, and status.

architecture.label: Owned resolution
architecture.detail: An operations user reviews assistance, takes action, and records the outcome.

guardrails: The public walkthrough uses synthetic scenarios rather than customer operational data.
Copilot assistance supports triage; a named operations owner remains accountable for resolution.
Production deployments need environment-specific security roles, data-loss prevention, monitoring, and escalation policy.
limitations: The published experience is a prototype and reference pattern, not a production freight system.
Connectors, schemas, service-level rules, and escalation logic require environment-specific configuration.
The repository does not establish measured operational improvement or production adoption.

provenance.label: Freight Triage Control Tower public repository
provenance.note: Public README, implementation files, synthetic scenario content, and hosted prototype are the evidence base for this entry.

visual.alt: A freight exception signal becomes a structured Dataverse item, appears in a control tower, and is closed by an accountable owner.

article.title: Turn freight exceptions into owned work
article.dek: A control-tower prototype reframes shipment signals as visible, aging, assignable work instead of another thread in an inbox.

releases.title: Warranty + Claims Operations
releases.summary: A Power Platform accelerator for structuring warranty and claims intake, review, supporting flows, and human-owned decisions.
releases.originalState: Warranty and claims work can span inconsistent intake, supporting documents, policy checks, status questions, and handoffs that are difficult to trace as one case.
releases.delivered: The public accelerator packages Dataverse tables, Canvas Apps, Power Automate flows, and Copilot Studio agents as a starting point for warranty and claims operations.
releases.outcome: The design is intended to create a more consistent case record, guide information gathering, and keep approval or exception decisions with accountable people.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: more consistent claims intake and review with visible status, supporting context, and human-owned decisions.

capabilities: Defines Dataverse structures for warranty and claims workflow data.
Provides Canvas App experiences for intake and operations review.
Uses flows to coordinate repeatable process steps and notifications.
Demonstrates Copilot Studio agents for guided questions and assistance.

architecture.label: Claim intake
architecture.detail: A Canvas App or guided conversation captures the claim and supporting context.

architecture.label: Dataverse case
architecture.detail: Structured tables hold the case, evidence, status, and relationships.

architecture.label: Flows and agents
architecture.detail: Automation and Copilot Studio assistance support routing and information gathering.

architecture.label: Human decision
architecture.detail: An authorized reviewer remains responsible for approval, exception handling, and final disposition.

guardrails: Copilot Studio assistance does not replace policy, legal, financial, or approval authority.
Consequential claim decisions remain with authorized reviewers.
Deployers must configure security roles, data retention, audit, connector policy, and jurisdiction-specific requirements.
limitations: The accelerator is a starting point and requires tailoring to policy, product, region, and operating model.
The public repository does not establish measured savings, accuracy, or production performance.
Document verification, fraud controls, integrations, and exception policy require additional implementation.

provenance.label: Warranty + Claims Operations public repository
provenance.note: Public README, solution inventory, agent definitions, app assets, and flow guidance are the evidence base for this entry.

visual.alt: A claim moves from guided intake into a Dataverse case, through flows and agent assistance, to an authorized human decision.

article.title: Keep claims assistance separate from claims authority
article.dek: A Power Platform accelerator structures intake and review while preserving the human decision boundary that matters.

releases.title: Prompt Escape
releases.summary: A multiplayer prompt-engineering escape room that turns clearer instructions, constraints, iteration, and creativity into a playable team challenge.
releases.originalState: Prompting concepts can stay abstract when learners only read examples instead of working through a shared problem with constraints, feedback, and room to iterate.
releases.delivered: The public project delivers a multiplayer escape-room game in which teams use prompts, clues, constraints, and iteration to progress through AI-assisted challenges.
releases.outcome: The experience is designed to make prompt quality discussable and memorable through practice, comparison, and team reflection.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: an experiential way for teams to practice clearer prompts, constraints, iteration, and collaborative problem solving.

capabilities: Packages prompt-engineering concepts as a multiplayer game.
Uses clues and constraints to reward clearer instructions and iteration.
Supports team play and discussion rather than an isolated tutorial.
Provides public source and a hosted game experience.

architecture.label: Team challenge
architecture.detail: Players enter a shared scenario with a goal, clues, and constraints.

architecture.label: Prompt attempt
architecture.detail: The team writes and refines instructions for the challenge.

architecture.label: Game response
architecture.detail: The application returns challenge feedback and progression state.

architecture.label: Team reflection
architecture.detail: Players compare approaches and decide how to improve the next attempt.

guardrails: The game is a learning experience, not a benchmark of a person or model.
Facilitators should avoid entering sensitive, personal, or proprietary information into prompts.
AI responses are part of the challenge and should be treated as fallible output.
limitations: Game behavior can vary with model configuration and service availability.
The experience does not measure durable skill improvement or workplace outcomes.
Facilitation, access, and deployment setup may be needed for a group session.

provenance.label: Prompt Escape public repository
provenance.note: Public README, game source, challenge content, and hosted experience are the evidence base for this entry.

visual.alt: A team challenge leads to a prompt attempt, game feedback, and team reflection before another iteration.

article.title: Teach prompting as a team sport
article.dek: A multiplayer escape room makes instructions, constraints, iteration, and reflection part of the learning loop.

releases.title: Copilot Studio + MCP Lab
releases.summary: A hands-on public lab for deploying a small Model Context Protocol tool and connecting it to GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Studio.
releases.originalState: MCP concepts can be difficult to connect to practice when the protocol, server deployment, tool definition, client configuration, and invocation path are learned separately.
releases.delivered: The public lab uses a deliberately small joke-server example to walk through an MCP tool, deployment, and connection from both GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Studio.
releases.outcome: The lab is designed to give builders a bounded end-to-end reference they can inspect before adapting the pattern to a real tool.

valueEvidence.statement: Designed value: a compact end-to-end MCP reference that makes server, tool, client, and invocation responsibilities easier to see.

capabilities: Implements a small public MCP server and callable tool.
Documents deployment and connection steps for the lab.
Shows the same tool pattern from GitHub Copilot and Copilot Studio clients.
Keeps the sample domain intentionally low-risk so the integration path stays visible.

architecture.label: Copilot client
architecture.detail: A user invokes the configured tool from GitHub Copilot or Copilot Studio.

architecture.label: MCP request
architecture.detail: The client sends a protocol request using the published tool contract.

architecture.label: Tool server
architecture.detail: The deployed sample server executes the bounded joke operation.

architecture.label: User response
architecture.detail: The client presents the tool result for the user to accept, ignore, or continue from.

guardrails: The sample tool is deliberately non-consequential and does not perform business writes.
The user chooses whether to invoke the tool and how to use its response.
Real tools require authentication, authorization, input validation, logging, and least-privilege design beyond the sample.
limitations: The lab demonstrates a narrow sample tool rather than a production MCP operating model.
Cloud deployment, client capabilities, and configuration steps can change over time.
The example does not establish enterprise security, scale, reliability, or support guarantees.

provenance.label: Copilot Studio + MCP Lab public repository
provenance.note: Public README, MCP server source, deployment assets, and client setup guidance are the evidence base for this entry.

visual.alt: A Copilot client sends an MCP request to a bounded tool server and presents the result back to the user.

article.title: Use a tiny tool to see the whole MCP path
article.dek: A deliberately small joke server makes the protocol boundary, deployment step, client connection, and user invocation easy to inspect.
